_comment: Every blast that has actually reached the league. Nothing else knows this: recaps.json records what has been written, not what has been sent, and the two are not the same file for a reason. The routine appends here after a send and commits, so the next run can tell whether the piece it is about to lead with has already been in somebody's inbox. blast-status.mjs reads it.

sent[].subject: the subject line as it went out
sent[].lead: slug of the article the blast led with, or null
sent[].alsoSent: slugs carried in the 'Also this week' section, which count as sent
sent[].recap: {season, week} of the recap it carried, or null
sent[].to: number of league addresses it reached
sent[].sha256: sha256 of the HTML body, so a resend is identifiable
sent[].note: anything a later reader would need to know

sent.subject: Re: DFFL Week 2: The Steepest Fall on the Board
sent.note: The routine sent this to Drew alone at 23:10Z under the old approval flow; Drew forwarded it to the other ten eleven minutes later. Recorded as the league send because that is what the league received. Dominick Reyes was not on that list.

sent.subject: DFFL Week 3: One Game Was on the Bench
sent.note: Sent early, on the Tuesday rather than waiting for the Saturday blast, because every week 2 game was final. All twelve in To at Drew's instruction rather than the usual eleven in BCC. First send to include Dominick Reyes. The 'Also this week' section was suppressed: both pieces it would have carried went out on 19 September.
